summary: 44-year-old woman on day 1 after total thyroidectomy with perioral tingling, carpopedal spasm, positive Chvostek sign, adjusted calcium 1.78 mmol/L, PTH undetectable, QTc 490 ms. Symptomatic hypocalcaemia: IV calcium gluconate with cardiac monitoring, check/correct magnesium, oral calcium + alfacalcidol.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Tingling around the mouth and hand cramps after thyroid surgery
inputs.hpi: Day 1 after total thyroidectomy with central neck dissection for papillary carcinoma. Since this morning tingling around the lips and in the fingertips, now painful cramping of both hands. Voice normal. Neck wound comfortable, no swelling.

exam.general: Carpopedal spasm, Chvostek sign positive. Neck wound flat and dry.

surgicalHistory: Total thyroidectomy and central neck dissection (yesterday)

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Symptomatic post-surgical hypocalcaemia (hypoparathyroidism) after total thyroidectomy
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Symptomatic hypocalcaemia (adjusted Ca 1.78, PTH undetectable, prolonged QTc) on day 1 after total thyroidectomy — post-surgical hypoparathyroidism. IV calcium gluconate with cardiac monitoring, IV magnesium, then oral calcium and alfacalcidol; recheck calcium in 4–6 h.

emergencyLevel.note: Symptomatic hypocalcaemia with QT prolongation needs immediate treatment.
emergencyLevel.knownGapNote: Triage priority_24_48h (score 25, post-op only): no rule for tingling/tetany/hypocalcaemia and lab values are not read by adaptiveTriage.
emergencyLevel.proposedFix: Add post-thyroidectomy hypocalcaemia rules: symptoms (perioral tingling, carpopedal spasm) and adjusted calcium below range → urgent; IV calcium gluconate + ECG prompt.

redFlags.knownGapNote: No web engine reads the adjusted calcium 1.78 mmol/L or the symptoms; E89.2 maps to no protocol.

mustInclude.note: SfE: symptomatic or severe acute hypocalcaemia is treated with IV calcium gluconate under cardiac monitoring.
mustInclude.knownGapNote: No IV calcium gluconate anywhere (only inside the elective thyroidectomy operative template, which does not fire here).

guideline.name: Society for Endocrinology emergency guidance — acute hypocalcaemia in adults
guideline.section: Symptomatic or severe hypocalcaemia: IV calcium gluconate with cardiac monitoring; check and correct magnesium; oral calcium and active vitamin D for post-surgical hypoparathyroidism
guideline.citation: Turner J, Gittoes N, Selby P; Society for Endocrinology Clinical Committee. Society for Endocrinology Endocrine Emergency Guidance: Emergency management of acute hypocalcaemia in adult patients. Endocr Connect. 2016;5:G7–G8.

rationale: Post-operative metabolic emergency. The CC template "Post-op follow-up (routine)" is what a ward clinician would pick; the vitals are normal, so escalation must come from the symptoms and the calcium result.
